blocks.x: MedTech sells outcomes and must prove them: connected devices generate telemetry that feeds service revenue, clinical evidence and regulatory post-market surveillance. The device-to-evidence loop is an engineering product, and EU MDR/CRA raise its bar. This page is the operating picture: what runs, what strains, and which capabilities move the numbers that decide the margin.

The work concentrates in device provisioning/ota, service dispatch, vigilance reporting, with clinical evidence assembly close behind. Volume grows on every path; the decision layer has not kept up. That gap is measurable, and it is the work.
where the friction concentrates, Medical Devices & MedTech edition:

items: Device fleets unconnected
Installed base lacks provisioning/OTA; service runs on reactive dispatch and field guesswork.
Post-market surveillance manual
MDR vigilance and performance data assembled manually; signal detection late.
Device security rising bar
EU CRA/MDR cybersecurity duties land on fleets with legacy firmware; SBOMs unknown.
Clinical evidence generation slow
Real-world device performance data underused for evidence packs.
Service economics opaque
Service cost per device unknown; contracts priced on tradition.
UDI/provenance trails weak
Device UDI/provenance evidence manual across the chain.

blocks.x: The proof in Medical Devices & MedTech is a working system on a real workflow. These are the builds that go live:

items: Device fleet platform
provisioning, OTA and telemetry for installed base
Device security program
SBOMs, signed firmware and vulnerability SLAs
Vigilance pipeline
device telemetry + complaints into signal detection
Evidence generation
real-world performance data into evidence packs
Service economics
cost per device instrumented; contracts repriced
